blocks.x: Supply Chain Risk & Continuity exists because a specific failure keeps repeating: multi-tier supply is opaque; disruptions surface as missed deliveries; re-planning takes weeks; ESG/provenance obligations add evidence duties.
Multi-tier supply is opaque; disruptions surface as missed deliveries; re-planning takes weeks; ESG/provenance obligations add evidence duties.

The pattern behind Supply Chain Risk & Continuity: decisions that should be systematized are still assembled by hand — one document, one queue, one meeting at a time. This solution replaces the assembly with a governed composition.

We build the risk-sensing control tower: multi-tier supplier telemetry, disruption early warning with scenario playbooks, autonomous re-planning within policy, and the provenance/evidence layer for regulated claims.

blocks.x: Supply Chain Risk & Continuity composes Dataq Nexus, Dataq Ledger — platforms with documented controls and evidence packs, so governance is part of the runtime. The pattern is in delivery now in Logistics & Supply Chain, Manufacturing & Industrial, Retail & Consumer Goods, Agriculture & Food Systems.

Method over magic in Supply Chain Risk & Continuity: the problem gets a CFO-unit statement and a signed baseline; the design gets a written risk envelope; the pilot gets falsifiable criteria; the rollout gets whatever the evidence supports. The engagement is instrumented like production, because it is production: gates, named owners, and a weekly cadence your control owner can forward. For Supply Chain Risk & Continuity, that discipline is not optional — it is the engagement model.

Every Supply Chain Risk & Continuity value case is written against named movements; the list below is the shape of that case, priced against your baseline during the diagnostic — never a promise from a brochure.
